status.obsolete_3ms_cpu_p95: different delayed composite scope; not a whole-renderer requirement
status.scope: B3 whole-renderer reference on one machine, not isolated RenderGraph overhead or pixel parity. Both B3 profiles explicitly disable the packed source AO channel while preserving source bytes/materials. Renderer: Neutral, post-tonemap FXAA, consumer IBL cook, offscreen. Godot: native AgX, pre-tonemap FXAA, RGBE-quantized panorama and native BRDF/prefilter/PCF/depth-prepass/batching/presentation. Godot main-camera frustum culling disabled is the primary reference; native shadow-caster filtering remains. Main-camera frustum culling enabled is supplementary. Engine counters and planned Graph draws are distinct. Both full-scene lighting profiles disable source AO contribution following the reference default; all ORM pixels and material references are retained. CPU active host elapsed excludes explicit yield waits but includes polling and possible OS descheduling; Whole-process charged CPU/N uses identical Windows accounting over N stationary route iterations in both engines, sums all threads and includes mandatory planning/record/submit/poll/retire/return as well as benchmark bookkeeping. It is an aggregate mean, never a per-frame p95 or a rendering-only efficiency ratio. Godot additionally includes scripts/physics/engine/presentation. Its pre/post draw elapsed covers native lowering, submit/present and ring wait/retire; setup and delayed viewport observations remain separate with no producer ID. Renderer full ROI including final drain, phase elapsed, explicit yields and wall/N remain reported. Timestamp/query and native CPU timer observations are opt-in and may affect cost. Iteration intervals include pipeline backpressure from an earlier submitted frame; per-frame build-to-observed-completion latency is never converted to FPS. Neither engine measures scanout/input latency. GPU correctness, final resource release, zero allocation and B5 window/interaction acceptance are separate. CPU affinity/QoS is declared in cpu_policy; a controlled CPU subset is distinct from the default scheduler.

limits: B3 whole-renderer reference on one machine, not isolated RenderGraph overhead or pixel parity. Both B3 profiles explicitly disable the packed source AO channel while preserving source bytes/materials. Renderer: Neutral, post-tonemap FXAA, consumer IBL cook, offscreen. Godot: native AgX, pre-tonemap FXAA, RGBE-quantized panorama and native BRDF/prefilter/PCF/depth-prepass/batching/presentation. Godot main-camera frustum culling disabled is the primary reference; native shadow-caster filtering remains. Main-camera frustum culling enabled is supplementary. Engine counters and planned Graph draws are distinct. Both full-scene lighting profiles disable source AO contribution following the reference default; all ORM pixels and material references are retained. CPU active host elapsed excludes explicit yield waits but includes polling and possible OS descheduling; Whole-process charged CPU/N uses identical Windows accounting over N stationary route iterations in both engines, sums all threads and includes mandatory planning/record/submit/poll/retire/return as well as benchmark bookkeeping. It is an aggregate mean, never a per-frame p95 or a rendering-only efficiency ratio. Godot additionally includes scripts/physics/engine/presentation. Its pre/post draw elapsed covers native lowering, submit/present and ring wait/retire; setup and delayed viewport observations remain separate with no producer ID. Renderer full ROI including final drain, phase elapsed, explicit yields and wall/N remain reported. Timestamp/query and native CPU timer observations are opt-in and may affect cost. Iteration intervals include pipeline backpressure from an earlier submitted frame; per-frame build-to-observed-completion latency is never converted to FPS. Neither engine measures scanout/input latency. GPU correctness, final resource release, zero allocation and B5 window/interaction acceptance are separate. CPU affinity/QoS is declared in cpu_policy; a controlled CPU subset is distinct from the default scheduler.
CPU budget uses worst independent run aggregate mean, not any per-frame p95, stability ceiling or identical-work efficiency guarantee.
Godot script/physics/presentation, worker parallelism, native blocking waits and unexposed producer IDs differ from Renderer offscreen poll/yield policy.
Boundary counters and script endpoint brackets preserve finite acquisition/skew costs. No subtraction of poll or inferred wall-minus-CPU wait.
Detailed timer/query off/on includes run variability; baseline callback/sample bookkeeping remains in both. Shipping Renderer library has no new clock/probe dependency.
Only endpoint host/GPU snapshots; desktop background load, clocks/thermal drift, active native swapchain image count and actual GPU occupancy were not continuously traced.
No physical VRAM residency, native OOM/device-loss injection, other hardware, long soak, Bloom/B4, scanout/input latency or full B5 interaction guarantee.
AgX addition and Lumberyard appearance changes remain outside this task.

identity.contract: Forward+ Vulkan release template; runtime glTF full exterior; generated tangents, uncompressed ImageTexture material images; no LOD/occlusion, optional frustum culling; windowed 1080p vsync off; fixed frame-indexed route. B2 retains base-only PNG images, authored AO, constant ambient .03, no IBL/shadow/AA, linear exposure1. B3 explicitly generates full PNG mip chains before warmup, renormalizing only normal-map coarser levels, and verifies actual native readbacks, base bytes and shared material references. Renderer retains authored DDS mip chains; Godot generated mip pixels are not equivalent. B3 disables source AO maps while retaining all source bytes/materials; cap4 static IBL strength3, four 2048-effective CSM splits/PCF/no PCSS, native AgX exposure2 and FXAA, no Bloom/extra effects. Godot's BRDF, prefilter, shadow filter, depth prepass, batching, mip chain and presentation differ from Renderer; AgX and pre-tonemap FXAA differ from Renderer Neutral and post-tonemap FXAA.

sun.units: Scene-linear benchmark irradiance; not measured lux or calibrated daylight.

preprocess.formula: c=max(decoded linear RGB,0); L=dot(c,coefficients); c*=min(1,cap/max(L,1e-20)); source texels before resampling/prefilter, then strength. Bright-source suppression, not physical sun removal.

ibl.mapping: u=fract(0.5+atan2(direction.z,direction.x)/(2*pi)); v=acos(clamp(direction.y,-1,1))/pi; source top row v=0; sample inverse R_y(yaw)*direction; repeat U, clamp V.

output.order: Linear HDR -> external Bloom if enabled -> multiply by 2^exposure_ev -> PBR Neutral -> sRGB OETF exactly once -> RGB8 round nearest, alpha 1.

acceptance.threshold_calibration: Before each acceptance: same API >=3 repeats, both APIs and known material/sRGB/alpha/shadow errors; freeze absolute/relative RGB/HDR, differing-pixel count and named ROI thresholds with settings hash. cpu_scope_comparison.budget_rule: 0.5ms * ceil(max(all/timing-0 independent run process-charged CPU/frame means)/0.5ms); cohort objective, never a per-frame p95
instrumentation_limits: Boundary counters are sequential, not atomic. First return packing can fall inside and last packing outside.

Godot worker count is configured -1 and not script-exposed per run; separate verbose probe observed20/6; actual GPU occupancy and swapchain image count unobserved.
